title: Pace the Meadow build by live GPU feedback, not numbers tuned on one phone
context: The recolour amendment (local branch mitosis/meadow-recolour-amend, 6e37ae7, not pushed) paced the scene build with an 8 ms processor budget. Emulator A/B (twice each, idle Mac) and a Note10+ trace showed the budget lets about 85-90 cheap plant-atlas steps run in one frame, queuing 55-77 ms of GPU bakes on the Note10+ (every 10.17 miss: 100-122 ms frames waiting behind them) and about 100 ms on the emulator. A fixed cap of 4 was approved, then shown by replaying the phone trace to push scene-ready to about 1.3 s; a cap of 32 was proposed. The owner rejected tuning to a single phone, and asked whether to lower quality instead; ongoing drawing already holds 60 fps on the Note10+ (11 of 12 cases), so the failure is one-time preparation, not per-frame quality.
options: fixed per-frame cap (4 or 32) tuned on the Note10+
frame-timing feedback (reports arrive about once a second in release)
GPU back-pressure: batch bakes, wait for a GPU completion signal, grow or shrink the batch; processor budget as half the display's frame interval
lower Meadow quality (sway, reflections, density) on weaker devices
outcome: GPU back-pressure with a processor budget derived from the display refresh rate, probed first on the Note10+, lab emulator and lab Mac VM, then specced for approval and dispatched with mitosis. Quality step-down for ongoing animation is deferred: only if necessary and only when the owner asks for it.
